items.name: PCB trace width (IPC-2221)
items.doc: Trace width that carries a given current at a given temperature rise, from the IPC-2221 equation, for outer and inner layers in 1 oz and 2 oz copper.
items.notes: I = k · ΔT^0.44 · A^0.725 with the cross-section A in mil², k = 0.048 for outer and 0.024 for inner layers, and 35 µm of copper per oz. A first estimate: neighbouring traces, vias, air flow and planes change the real temperature rise, so test high currents.
items.source: IPC-2221 (Generic Standard on Printed Board Design), current-carrying capacity equation I = k·ΔT^0.44·A^0.725

items.name: Preferred values E3 to E24
items.doc: The IEC 60063 preferred values of resistors and capacitors from E3 to E24, one decade, with the series each value belongs to.
items.notes: Multiply a value by a power of ten for the other decades. Typical tolerances: E6 ±20 %, E12 ±10 %, E24 ±5 %. A dot marks the series a value belongs to.
items.source: IEC 60063 (preferred number series for resistors and capacitors)

items.name: Preferred values E48 to E192
items.doc: The IEC 60063 preferred values of precision resistors and capacitors from E48 to E192, one decade, with the series each value belongs to.
items.notes: Multiply a value by a power of ten for the other decades. Typical tolerances: E48 ±2 %, E96 ±1 %, E192 ±0.5 % and tighter. A dot marks the series a value belongs to; every E48 value is also in E96, and every E96 value in E192.
items.source: IEC 60063 (preferred number series for resistors and capacitors)

items.name: Capacitor codes
items.doc: Capacitor markings: the picofarad code (104 = 100 nF), R and RKM notation (4R7, 4p7, 2n2), tolerance letters and the two-character rated-voltage codes (1H = 50 V). Several parts of one marking can be read together ("104K 1H").
items.source: IEC 60062:2016 (capacitance codes and tolerance letters); the voltage codes are a convention of the part-numbering systems of TDK, Nichicon, Panasonic and Murata, not of IEC 60062; KEMET and Vishay ceramic capacitor datasheets

voltages.note: Murata lists 3F as 3.15 kV, TDK as 3 kV.
voltages.note_en: Murata lists 3F as 3.15 kV, TDK as 3 kV.

notes: Ceramic and film capacitors: the code is in picofarads - 104 = 100 000 pF = 100 nF. Aluminium electrolytic part numbers use microfarads (101 = 100 µF); that reading is not offered.
Below 10 pF tolerance letters mean absolute pF (C = ±0.25 pF), from 10 pF up they mean percent.
Voltage codes come from maker part-numbering systems and are not part of IEC 60062; some makers deviate (Murata writes YA for 35 V).
Codes and letters that only one source lists are not decoded; the decoder says so.

items.name: Ceramic capacitor temperature codes
items.doc: EIA-198 temperature characteristics of ceramic capacitors: class 1 codes such as C0G or U2J (temperature coefficient and tolerance in ppm/K) and class 2 codes such as X7R or Y5V (category temperature range and capacitance change), in both directions.
items.source: EIA-198 code letters as printed in the Vishay general information on ceramic disc capacitors and in the Murata, KEMET and TDK ceramic capacitor catalogues

notes: C0G (NP0) is the most stable class 1 dielectric: 0 ± 30 ppm/K.
Class 2 codes describe only the temperature range and the change over temperature; DC bias and ageing reduce the capacitance further.
Y5V and Z5U are class 2 here; some manufacturers call them class 3.
Letters and digits that only one source lists are not decoded; the decoder says so.

items.name: Inductor colour code
items.doc: Colour bands of inductors in microhenries: the four-band EIA style and the five-band military style (wide silver first band, gold as the decimal point), read and written in both directions.
items.source: Bourns colour-code markings for inductors (EIA and military tables) and MIL-PRF-15305 for RF coils; IEC 60062 defines no inductor colour code; E-series from IEC 60063

notes: Inductor colour codes are maker and military conventions; IEC 60062 only covers resistors. Values are in µH.
A wide silver first band marks a military (MIL-PRF-15305) coil; gold inside the value bands is then the decimal point.
Without the wide silver band (EIA style), gold in the third band means ×0.1 and silver ×0.01.
Only gold (±5 %) and silver (±10 %) are decoded as tolerance; other tolerance colours are not cross-checked in the sources.

items.name: Resistor colour code
items.doc: Colour bands of resistors per IEC 60062: 3 to 6 bands read and written in both directions (two or three significant figures, multiplier, tolerance and temperature coefficient). Writing a value picks the nearest standard value of the series that fits the tolerance.
items.source: IEC 60062:2016 (marking codes for resistors and capacitors) with COR1:2016 and AMD1:2019, Table 1; the older tolerance colours from the resistor colour-code notes of Panasonic and TT Electronics; E-series from IEC 60063

notes: Read from the end where the bands start; the tolerance band is at least 1.5 times as wide as the others (IEC 60062, corrigendum 2016). Gold, silver and pink never stand first.
Older charts use grey = ±0.05 % and give orange and yellow no tolerance; IEC 60062:2016 uses grey ±0.01 %, orange ±0.05 % and yellow ±0.02 %. Check the datasheet of precision resistors.
Pink (×0.001) is new in IEC 60062:2016 for very low resistances.
A single black band marks a zero-ohm jumper.
The temperature coefficient band only exists together with three significant figures (six bands).
Displayed colours are illustrations only.

items.name: SMD resistor codes
items.doc: Markings of chip resistors: the 3-digit and 4-digit codes, the R notation (4R7, R47, 1L5) and the EIA-96 code (two digits for the E96 value plus a multiplier letter). The input is auto-detected; writing a value lists every marking that can express it.
items.source: IEC 60062:2016 (RKM code, three- and four-character codes); EIA-96 marking tables of Yageo, Bourns, Venkel and TT Electronics; E96 values from IEC 60063

notes: The two EIA-96 digits are an index, not the value: 01 means 100, 68 means 499.
3-digit codes: the last digit is the number of zeros, so 100 = 10 Ω, not 100 Ω.
R (and L for milliohm) marks the decimal point: 4R7 = 4.7 Ω, R47 = 0.47 Ω, 1L5 = 1.5 mΩ.
Very small chips (0402 and smaller) are usually unmarked.
Some makers use R, S or H as extra EIA-96 letters with conflicting meanings; they are not decoded - check the datasheet.
